messages.subject: advice on formula/model
parts:
Dear R-inla discussion group,
I am using rw2d models for spatial data of coastal seabird densities. Until now, I fitted models for each survey (n=3, all in the same area) separately. However, although birds may move along the coast, they are generally located at certain water depths. Therefore, I'd like to use this shared information between surveys - ultimately to estimate gaps in less complete surveys.

I tried this:

   ncol = length(unique(x))
   nrow = length(unique(y))
   n = ncol * nrow
   node1 = c(1:n, rep(NA,2*n))
   node2 = c(rep(NA,n), 1:n, rep(NA,n))
   node3 = c(rep(NA,2*n), 1:n)               # nodes for the rw2d model; each set of nodes corresponding to a survey, others set to NA
   ftrip = factor(c(1:3), each=n)              # to get an intercept for each survey

   formula = count ~ depth + f(node1, model="rw2d", ncol=ncol, nrow=nrow) + f(node2, model="rw2d", ncol=ncol, nrow=nrow) + f(node3, model="rw2d", ncol=ncol, nrow=nrow) + ftrip -1
  
   result = inla(formula, data=data, family="nbinomial", offset=offsetter)


I'd like to have your opinion about whether this is a good idea in general and/or if there are better ways of doing this.

Thanks in advance!
Rob

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] advice on formula/model
parts:
On 23/05/13 21:22, Rob van Bemmelen wrote:
> I am using rw2d models for spatial data of coastal seabird densities.
> Until now, I fitted models for each survey (n=3, all in the same area)
> separately. However, although birds may move along the coast, they are
> generally located at certain water depths. Therefore, I'd like to use
> this shared information between surveys - ultimately to estimate gaps in
> less complete surveys.

Yes, the essence of this seems good. If you also want also want to
borrow strength by assuming that all three surveys should have the same
precision parameter for the rw2d effect, you can use just a single f(),
and specify that there are three independent replications of the same model:

node = rep(1:n, times=3) ## Each node is used once per survey
repl = rep(1:3, each=n) ## Three surveys, each with n nodes
ftrip = factor(c(1:3), each=n) # to get an intercept for each survey

formula = count ~ depth + f(node, model="rw2d", ncol=ncol, nrow=nrow,
replicate=repl) + ftrip -1

/Finn
